dataRules.bridgeMarkers: NOAA Coast Pilot or USCG rounded reference points, not surveyed span axes
dataRules.access: Only documented public sidewalk and park area; no parking or exact sightline guarantee

viewpoints.name: 95th Street Bridge approaches
viewpoints.short: Best for watching a bridge lift
viewpoints.coordinateNote: Rounded bridge location is an orientation reference, NOT an identified public standing spot or parking entrance.
viewpoints.visit: This working bridge marks the meeting of South Chicago and the East Side. From a legal public sidewalk near the crossing, watch how two giant leaves swing upward to clear a vessel. Sidewalk access, maintenance closures and safe waiting space must be checked on arrival.
viewpoints.mapsQuery: 95th Street Bridge over Calumet River, Chicago Illinois

viewpoints.name: Calumet Park lakefront
viewpoints.coordinateNote: General park area marker, NOT a surveyed lakefront entrance or promised view into the channel.
viewpoints.visit: This Chicago Park District lakefront park is a public alternative near the harbor. A ship may be distant or out of view from a particular part of the shoreline; it is not a close-range bridge viewpoint. Check park rules and access before visiting.

bridges.name: Ewing Avenue / 92nd Street
bridges.summary: Near the river mouth, where ships enter from Lake Michigan. A bascule leaf pivots about a trunnion; this is not a status monitor.

bridges.name: 95th Street
bridges.summary: The celebrated ship-watching bridge. Two counterweighted leaves rise to make vertical clearance for a large vessel.

bridges.name: 100th Street
bridges.summary: An older trunnion bascule crossing in the industrial corridor; position is an approximate chart reference, not surveyed span geometry.

bridges.name: 106th Street
bridges.summary: A large double-leaf bascule structure built for the river's deep-draft traffic. Operational state is not known from this static catalog.

bridges.name: Torrence Avenue
bridges.summary: Unlike a bascule span, a vertical-lift span travels upward between towers. Older references may describe different nearby Torrence crossings; this point is for broad river orientation only.
